accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT identified as a cause of urban flooding?
accepted.x: Urban flooding is associated with unplanned concretisation, blocked natural drains and canals, encroached lakes and extreme rainfall. Expansion of natural drainage channels is not a listed cause.
accepted.tq: Find the option that reverses a stated cause.
accepted.sec: Urban flooding - causes and cases

accepted.s: The urban flood of 26 July 2005 is associated with which city?
accepted.x: Mumbai experienced the major urban flood on 26 July 2005.
accepted.tq: Direct city-and-date recall.
accepted.sec: Urban flooding - causes and cases

accepted.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Mumbai — 26 July 2005 urban flood
2. Chennai — December 2015 urban flood
3. Vijayawada — Budameru-related urban flooding
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
accepted.x: All three pairs are correctly matched. The Vijayawada case is associated with flooding linked to the Budameru rivulet.
accepted.tq: Use a familiar pair to eliminate mismatched city-event combinations.
accepted.sec: Urban flooding - causes and cases

accepted.s: Which combination correctly describes Andhra Pradesh's City Flood Alert platform announced in July 2026?
o: A drought-monitoring platform developed by APTRANSCO and ISRO
An AI platform of RTGS, APSDMA and IIT Gandhinagar providing 48-hour rainfall forecasts and 6-hour flash-flood warnings
A cyclone-warning platform of IMD and the Navy providing 72-hour forecasts
A seismic-alert platform of GSI and IIT Hyderabad providing 24-hour earthquake warnings
accepted.x: The City Flood Alert is an AI platform developed by RTGS, APSDMA and IIT Gandhinagar. It provides 48-hour rainfall forecasts and 6-hour flash-flood warnings.
accepted.tq: Split the option into agency, technology and forecast-duration clues.
accepted.sec: Urban flooding - causes and cases

accepted.s: The first implementation of Andhra Pradesh's City Flood Alert platform was planned for which city?
accepted.x: The platform was first planned for Vijayawada and was subsequently proposed for all Urban Local Bodies.
accepted.tq: Direct first-location recall.
accepted.sec: Urban flooding - causes and cases

accepted.s: The City Flood Alert platform uses which combination of inputs for Vijayawada flood warnings?
o: Forest-fire maps and satellite night-light data
Satellite DEM and approximately 30 years of Budameru data
Ocean salinity data and 5 years of Krishna delta data
Seismic records and 30 years of rainfall data from the Eastern Ghats
accepted.x: The platform uses satellite-derived Digital Elevation Model data and approximately 30 years of Budameru data.
accepted.tq: Identify the exact data-source pair.
accepted.sec: Urban flooding - causes and cases

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Disaster)
 a. Bhopal gas tragedy
 b. Chernobyl disaster
 c. Fukushima Daiichi disaster
 d. Nuclear waste hazard

List-II (Agent or cause)
 i. Improper disposal of radioactive waste
 ii. Methyl isocyanate
 iii. Reactor No. 4 explosion and radioactive release
 iv. Earthquake-tsunami followed by reactor meltdowns

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Bhopal involved methyl isocyanate; Chernobyl involved the explosion of Reactor No. 4; Fukushima followed an earthquake and tsunami; improper disposal of radioactive waste is a separate nuclear hazard.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure agent pair and complete the elimination.
accepted.sec: Industrial and nuclear disasters - place, year, agent  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The Bhopal gas tragedy occurred at the Union Carbide plant during which period?
accepted.x: The Bhopal gas tragedy occurred on 2–3 December 1984 at the Union Carbide plant in Bhopal, Madhya Pradesh.
accepted.tq: Distinguish closely related disaster dates.
accepted.sec: Industrial and nuclear disasters - place, year, agent  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Chernobyl is correctly associated with which place and date?
accepted.x: The Chernobyl disaster occurred at Pripyat in Ukraine, then part of the USSR, on 26 April 1986.
accepted.tq: Match the disaster with its location and date.
accepted.sec: Industrial and nuclear disasters - place, year, agent  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The Fukushima Daiichi disaster was primarily triggered by which sequence?
o: Tropical cyclone followed by a dam burst
Earthquake and tsunami followed by reactor meltdowns
Volcanic eruption followed by a chemical leak
accepted.x: The Fukushima Daiichi disaster in Japan on 11 March 2011 followed an earthquake and tsunami, which led to reactor meltdowns.
accepted.tq: Test the correct cause-effect sequence.
accepted.sec: Industrial and nuclear disasters - place, year, agent  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Under the HSDPR scheme for 2021–26, which provision relates to health-sector CBRN readiness?
o: Ten tertiary and two secondary CBRN centres
Two tertiary and twenty secondary trauma centres
One tertiary and five secondary CBRN centres
Two tertiary and ten secondary CBRN medical management centres
accepted.x: The HSDPR scheme provides for setting up two tertiary and ten secondary CBRN medical management centres during 2021–26.
accepted.tq: Recall the paired institutional count.
accepted.sec: Industrial and nuclear disasters - place, year, agent  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The NIDM Southern Campus at Kondapalli is associated with which activity?
o: Conducting crop-weather surveys in drought-prone districts
Forecasting earthquakes in the Eastern Ghats
Preparing safety audits for chemical corridors and port clusters
Monitoring ocean currents in the Bay of Bengal
accepted.x: The NIDM Southern Campus at Kondapalli, Andhra Pradesh, prepares safety audits for chemical corridors and port clusters.
accepted.tq: Identify the institution from its specialised function.
accepted.sec: Industrial and nuclear disasters - place, year, agent  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding India's disaster vulnerability:
1. About 58.6% of India's landmass faces moderate-to-very-high earthquake risk.
2. More than 40 million hectares, approximately 12% of the area, is flood-prone.
3. About 68% of the cultivable area is vulnerable to drought.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements correctly represent the cited hazard shares for India.
accepted.tq: Check each numerical statement independently before selecting the coded combination.
accepted.sec: Vulnerability profile of India - hazard-prone states and area shares  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: According to the older coastline base used for the hazard estimates, approximately how much of India's coastline faces cyclones and tsunamis?
accepted.x: Approximately 5,700 km of the old 7,516.6 km coastline was considered exposed to cyclones and tsunamis.
accepted.tq: Separate the exposed length from the total and revised coastline figures.
accepted.sec: Vulnerability profile of India - hazard-prone states and area shares  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: What is the significance of the figure 11,098.81 km in relation to India's coastline?
o: It is the cyclone-prone length of the old coastline
It is the remeasured coastline length reported in December 2024
It is the length vulnerable to tsunamis alone
It is the length of the eastern coastline only
accepted.x: The coastline was remeasured to 11,098.81 km by the Ministry of Home Affairs in December 2024. Older hazard shares used the earlier base of 7,516.6 km.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between revised total and older hazard-share figures.
accepted.sec: Vulnerability profile of India - hazard-prone states and area shares  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the cyclone vulnerability of India?
o: Cyclones affect 13 coastal States or Union Territories and 84 coastal districts; Andhra Pradesh is identified as the most cyclone-prone state.
Cyclones affect only 9 coastal States and Andhra Pradesh is least affected on the east coast.
Cyclones affect 13 inland States and 84 districts, with Rajasthan as the most cyclone-prone state.
Cyclones affect 84 Union Territories and 13 coastal districts, with the west coast receiving most cyclones.
accepted.x: Cyclones affect 13 coastal States or Union Territories and 84 coastal districts. Andhra Pradesh is identified as the most cyclone-prone state, and the east coast receives far more cyclones than the west.
accepted.tq: Use composition, number and east-west comparison together.
accepted.sec: Vulnerability profile of India - hazard-prone states and area shares  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Assam alone has approximately how much flood-prone area?
accepted.x: Assam has approximately 31.05 lakh hectares of flood-prone area.
accepted.tq: Watch the placement of the decimal and the lakh unit.
accepted.sec: Vulnerability profile of India - hazard-prone states and area shares  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: According to the World Risk Index 2025, India is the world's second most vulnerable country after which country?
accepted.x: The World Risk Index 2025 places India as the second most vulnerable country, after the Philippines.
accepted.tq: Direct ranking recall.
accepted.sec: Vulnerability profile of India - hazard-prone states and area shares  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly classified as a biological disaster?
accepted.x: Epidemics, pandemics and pest attacks are biological disasters. Earthquakes are geophysical, cyclones are hydro-meteorological, and nuclear incidents are man-made or technological.
accepted.tq: Classify the example rather than the general term.
accepted.sec: Classification of disasters - natural vs man-made  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Class)
 a. Geological or geophysical
 b. Hydro-meteorological
 c. Climatological
 d. Man-made or technological

List-II (Example)
 i. Extreme temperatures
 ii. Chemical and industrial accidents
 iii. Earthquakes
 iv. Floods

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Earthquakes are geological or geophysical; floods are hydro-meteorological; extreme temperatures are climatological; and chemical and industrial accidents are man-made or technological.
accepted.tq: Start with the distinctive technological and geological examples.
accepted.sec: Classification of disasters - natural vs man-made  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which statement best expresses the relationship between hazard, vulnerability and disaster?
o: Only man-made hazards can become disasters when vulnerability is present.
Hazard + vulnerability always equals disaster, irrespective of exposure.
Vulnerability alone is a disaster, even without any hazard.
Hazard multiplied by vulnerability gives disaster; an earthquake in an empty desert may remain a hazard rather than become a disaster.
accepted.x: The relationship is expressed as Hazard × Vulnerability = Disaster. An earthquake in an uninhabited desert may be a hazard but not a disaster because significant vulnerability and exposure are absent.
accepted.tq: Apply the formula to the empty-desert example.
accepted.sec: Classification of disasters - natural vs man-made  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following is an emerging hazard identified in addition to conventional natural and technological hazards?
accepted.x: Cyber attacks, space weather and AI failures are identified as emerging hazards.
accepted.tq: Pick the item belonging to the emerging-hazard category.
accepted.sec: Classification of disasters - natural vs man-made  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about notified disasters eligible for SDRF or NDRF assistance:
1. The number of notified disasters became 14 after August 2026.
2. Heatwave and lightning were added on the advice of the Sixteenth Finance Commission.
3. Man-made calamities are included among the notified disasters.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The number rose to 14 after heatwave and lightning were added; no man-made calamity is notified for this purpose.
accepted.tq: Find the single false statement by checking the eligibility exception.
accepted.sec: Classification of disasters - natural vs man-made  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Landslides occur predominantly in which type of terrain?
accepted.x: Landslides occur mostly in hilly terrain.
accepted.tq: Direct terrain association.
accepted.sec: Landslides and avalanches - terrain, zones, rising frequency  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly identifies the major landslide zones mentioned for India?
o: The Thar Desert and the Indo-Gangetic plain
The Himalaya and the Western Ghats
The Sundarbans and the Rann of Kachchh
The Coromandel coast and the Deccan plateau only
accepted.x: Major landslide zones include the Himalaya, covering Jammu and Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand and the Northeast, and the Western Ghats, including Kerala, Konkan and the Nilgiris.
accepted.tq: Identify the paired physiographic zones.
accepted.sec: Landslides and avalanches - terrain, zones, rising frequency  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Avalanches in India are primarily associated with which region and States or Union Territories?
o: Eastern coast—Odisha, Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu
Western Ghats—Kerala, Goa, Karnataka and Tamil Nadu
Snow-bound Himalaya—Jammu and Kashmir, Ladakh, Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand
accepted.x: Avalanches are associated with the snow-bound Himalaya, particularly Jammu and Kashmir, Ladakh, Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand.
accepted.tq: Distinguish avalanche geography from landslide geography.
accepted.sec: Landslides and avalanches - terrain, zones, rising frequency  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following factors contributes to the increasing frequency of landslides?
o: Increase in forest cover on vulnerable slopes
accepted.x: Unregulated construction on unstable slopes is one of the factors increasing landslide frequency. Deforestation, road widening, cloudbursts and deglaciation are other cited factors.
accepted.tq: Select the human activity that increases slope instability.
accepted.sec: Landslides and avalanches - terrain, zones, rising frequency  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The diversion of approximately 43 hectares of land and approval for felling about 7,000 deodars are associated with which project-related landslide concern?
accepted.x: These figures are associated with road widening connected with the Char Dham project and its ecological and slope-stability concerns.
accepted.tq: Link the numerical environmental detail with the project name.
accepted.sec: Landslides and avalanches - terrain, zones, rising frequency  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which agency is the nodal agency for landslide studies in India?
accepted.x: The Geological Survey of India is the nodal agency for landslide studies.
accepted.tq: Identify the agency from its specialised mandate.
accepted.sec: Landslides and avalanches - terrain, zones, rising frequency  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following disasters in chronological order:
A. Latur earthquake
B. Bhuj earthquake
C. Odisha super cyclone
D. Indian Ocean tsunami
accepted.x: The correct sequence is Latur earthquake in 1993, Odisha super cyclone in 1999, Bhuj earthquake in 2001 and Indian Ocean tsunami in 2004.
accepted.tq: Fix the earliest and latest events, then arrange the middle events by year.
accepted.sec: Major disasters in India - year and place; hazard → region  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The Latur or Killari earthquake occurred on which date and in which State?
accepted.x: The Latur or Killari earthquake occurred on 30 September 1993 in Maharashtra.
accepted.tq: Direct date-and-place recall.
accepted.sec: Major disasters in India - year and place; hazard → region  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The Odisha super cyclone of October 1999 is associated particularly with which location?
accepted.x: The Odisha super cyclone occurred in October 1999 along the Odisha coast, particularly around Paradip.
accepted.tq: Match the disaster with its affected coastal region.
accepted.sec: Major disasters in India - year and place; hazard → region  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
accepted.x: The Chamoli glacier burst of 2021 occurred in Uttarakhand, not Himachal Pradesh. The other three pairs are correctly matched.
accepted.tq: Find the wrong place in a disaster-year-location chain.
accepted.sec: Major disasters in India - year and place; hazard → region  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The Dharali flash flood of 5 August 2025 occurred in which district and State?
accepted.x: The Dharali flash flood occurred on 5 August 2025 in Uttarkashi district of Uttarakhand.
accepted.tq: Combine the precise date with the location rather than only the State.
accepted.sec: Major disasters in India - year and place; hazard → region  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following hazard-to-region associations is correctly matched?
o: Cyclones — east coast; drought — Rajasthan and the Deccan interior
Drought — Western Ghats; earthquakes — east coast only
accepted.x: Cyclones are especially associated with the east coast, while drought is prominent in Rajasthan and the Deccan interior. Floods affect the Brahmaputra-Ganga plains, earthquakes the Himalaya and Kutch, and landslides the Himalaya and Western Ghats.
accepted.tq: Check both hazard and regional setting in each pair.
accepted.sec: Major disasters in India - year and place; hazard → region  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following statements about the Indian Ocean tsunami of 26 December 2004 is correct?
o: It affected Tamil Nadu, the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Kerala and Andhra Pradesh.
It affected only Gujarat and Maharashtra.
It affected only the western coast of India.
It was confined to the Himalayan States.
accepted.x: The Indian Ocean tsunami of 26 December 2004 affected Tamil Nadu, the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Kerala and Andhra Pradesh.
accepted.tq: Recall the affected-region list without confusing east and west coasts.
accepted.sec: Major disasters in India - year and place; hazard → region  [APPSC, GROUP-II]
